craft_notes: Sthāyin: contentment-sacrifice (tuṣṭi as the oblation: wasting sins, protecting all). Rows: row 3 (bliss-marked→daughter). Close: daughter (pārvatī as mountain's daughter — kinship closes the practice arc: the fierce text ends in family). Rejected: 'goddess' generic — killed: mountain's daughter kept (the text's own kin-name); 'purifies' — killed: wasting kept (kṣaya as wearing-away, gradual like v51's days).

lines: Sacrifice here, highest lady — contentment, bliss-marked:
wasting all sins, protecting all — mountain's daughter.
l4.sanskrit_cite: yāgo 'tra parameśāni tuṣṭir ānandalakṣaṇā | kṣapaṇāt sarvapāpānāṃ trāṇāt sarvasya pārvati

reads_against.argmap: What is the sacrifice? → Sacrifice is contentment itself — it wastes sins and protects all.
c1_essence: Sacrifice is contentment: wasting sins, protecting all.
reads_against.c1_rasa: vīra with śānta (resolve closing the practice arc)
